properties.description: A process-global that is secretly per-design cannot be added without accounting for it. An allowlist over runtime `static` / `thread_local!` / `lazy_static!` declarations across every crate's `src` tree: an unlisted global FAILS the build, and adding one costs a written reason why it is not per-design. Owed by rule:per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global from the moment it was set enforced (Anthony, 2026-08-09). BOUND, stated rather than left to be discovered: it detects DECLARATIONS only. It says nothing about whether a struct field is correctly scoped — the per-design metadata riding on ReflowService today (graph_path, write_gen, read_hint) is not a global, and moving it per-graph is cap:graph-registry's planned work rather than a violation. A second test guards the guard — an allowlist entry naming a global that no longer exists fails, because a stale exemption pre-authorises the name for whoever adds it back.
properties.findings: NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN, not assumed: a static planted in crates/reflow2-core/src/temporal.rs (a different crate from every allowlist entry) failed the check by name and line, and the file was reverted.
properties.name: A process-global that is secretly per-design cannot be added without accounting for it
